test: IDUI Test 04 (see PROTOCOL.md amendments A3 and A4)
tier: C - the owner judging rendered frames on the phone. Not Tier A, not Tier B.

source.query: select device, arm, constitution, count(*), sum((verdict='keep')::int), sum((verdict='reject')::int), count(distinct seed), count(distinct framing), min(judged_at), max(judged_at) from betta_verdicts group by device, arm, constitution order by min(judged_at)
source.access: publishable key, insert-only for anon under RLS, verdict constrained to keep or reject; rows are the owner's taps in the Betta Explorer WebView APK (~/Documents/betta-explorer-android, not part of this repository)
source.note: Rows tagged android-webview/<build> are that APK's; the untagged first block is the pre-0.7 explorer before the device column carried a build. One emulator row (id 409, build 0.9) was deleted before the owner installed 0.9; the 0.10 emulator run left none.

framing: one per row: the phone's own portrait framing, not one of the eight locked landscape compositions

rows.excluded_because: 0.8 showed a black screen on the owner's device; the owner rejected 34 black frames in one minute and reported the build. These are verdicts on a bug, not on the constitution. Excluded on that ground before this snapshot was taken, not after seeing the rate.

reading: The same arm C at the same constitution keeps at about a third on the phone against about a half on the Mac (keep-rate-20260908.json). Different framing, different pixel density, different pace of judging: render surface moves the number more than any arm did.
Every row is one seed; no seed was judged twice. Rejections are labelled by seed, so the set is a reject corpus the explorer keeps growing.
This is one judge's taste on one device. It is not evidence for or against the frozen claim, which is about validity.
